title: Dynamic windowing and sparse indexing to cut tail latency in dashboard streams
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our dashboard query API exhibits a pronounced tail latency for large pagination requests and high-cardinality tenants. Root causes from initial triage: wide time-window scans that bypass compact per-tenant indexes, inefficient materialization of ephemeral cursor state for long scans, and bursty traffic that evicts shared caches. This ticket proposes a combined server-side approach: adaptive 'dynamic windowing' that adjusts page/window size heuristically per-tenant and per-query signature; and lightweight 'sparse indexes' materialized for hot time windows to avoid full shard scans. Goals: reduce 99th percentile latency by at least 40% on affected endpoints and cut tokenized DB I/O for paginated dashboards by ~35% for top 10% tenants.
background: Observed in customer-facing SLO dashboards and internal telemetry: some tenants produce repeated deep-pagination patterns (export-like queries) which cause repeated full-scan index seeks. Console endpoints affected: /v1/dashboard/query, /v1/dashboard/explore, and the paginated export slice API. Previous mitigations (increasing cache TTL, prefetching first N pages) helped median latency but not tail. Related tickets: ENG-30482, ENG-34912, ENG-88776 (see dependencies).
proposal: 1) Dynamic windowing: introduce an adaptive page size controller that picks a window (page size + lookahead) based on tenant recent access pattern, query signature, and current CPU/IO headroom. Implemented as a low-latency decision at the query router layer with safe upper bounds to preserve resource isolation. 2) Sparse time-window indexes: create compact secondary indexes for 1h and 6h windows for high-activity tenant/shard keys. These indexes store pointers to bucketed aggregates to avoid scanning full event segments for common filters. 3) Read-path shaping: add tenant-aware routing to prefer warm replicas when serving deep-pagination and apply rate-limited background slice-merging to keep index fragmentation low. 4) Incremental rollout: start with a small cohort (10 tenants), synthetic load tests, perf benchmarks, then broader ramp. 5) Observability: add new metrics (window_choice, sparse_index_hit, downstream_scan_bytes) and dashboards and set an alert for regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile latency for /v1/dashboard/query reduced by >=40% for cohort tenants in canary tests
Average DB scan bytes per deep-pagination request reduced by >=30% in canary
No regression in median latency or error rate on other Console endpoints during canary
New metrics emitted (window_choice, sparse_index_hit_rate, slice_merge_duration) and visible in console-telemetry dashboard
Feature gate and rollout path documented and approved by SRE and Product

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Sparse index creation could increase write amplification. Mitigation: throttle background jobs and cap to top-k tenants by activity.
Risk: Dynamic windowing may increase per-request CPU if controller is expensive. Mitigation: keep decision logic O(1) with a small in-memory LRU of recent tenant signatures.
Risk: Unexpected regressions on other endpoints during rollout. Mitigation: feature-gate and gradual ramp with automated rollback criteria.
Risk: Storage overhead from sparse indexes. Mitigation: support TTL and compaction; only create for windows with high hit-rate observed in sampling period.
